title: Case: Business shipper disputes three import duty invoices raised against its account
context: A business account that ships textiles abroad with Gorsewick Arc has been invoiced for import duty and tax on three export shipments. Import billing at Gorsewick Arc owns those invoices; Business billing and the desk cannot open or amend them.
initial_request: Eleven years and roughly a van a day with Gorsewick Arc, and I am explaining who pays import duty to a helpdesk. It is written on the invoice. In English. It has been written on every invoice we have ever sent abroad. I am not interested in another 'we have passed it on'. What I want from you, in writing, today, is confirmation that all three invoices were raised in error and that credits totalling GBP 1,286.40 will be on the September statement. If I do not have that by close of business the August account goes unpaid and the contract goes out to tender. I imagine somebody there can do the sum on what that costs you.

events.body:
Thanks,
Yorick
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

events.from: Xanthe Abernathy, accounts director, Saltmarsh Looms (shipper)
events.body: Third time of asking. Invoices IMP-4388, IMP-3833 and IMP-3331 bill Saltmarsh Looms for destination duty and tax on DL-8750, DL-9335 and DL-4370. Our commercial invoice on every export states the buyer pays import charges. Explain or credit. Two previous portal queries on this (14 and 22 July) have had no reply.

events.to: Xanthe Abernathy, accounts director, Saltmarsh Looms (shipper)
events.body: Business billing: I can see the three import invoices on your account but I can't open them, they belong to Import billing. I can transfer you. Abernathy: You transferred me to them on Thursday. It rang out. Business billing: I'm sorry, a transfer is the only route I have to that team. Abernathy: So nobody who answers a phone can discuss an invoice you've sent me. Business billing: I can transfer you.

events.from: Xanthe Abernathy, accounts director, Saltmarsh Looms (shipper)
events.body: I'm told you coordinate. Coordinate this. Three import invoices, IMP-4388, IMP-3833, IMP-3331, on DL-8750, DL-9335, DL-4370, total GBP 1,286.40, all charged to us when our paperwork says the buyer pays. Import billing don't answer. The helpline transfers me to Import billing.

Saltmarsh Looms (Xanthe Abernathy) disputes IMP-4388, IMP-3833 and IMP-3331, raised on DL-8750, DL-9335 and DL-4370. He says the commercial invoices put import charges on the buyer and that three portal queries since 13 July are unanswered. Please review each invoice and reply to him.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.
My parcel DL-56715 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

Looked at DL-9335 only so far. The waybill terms on DL-9335 are recipient pays. The recipient declined the import charges at delivery on 13 July, and under the account terms declined charges revert to the shipper. So IMP-3833 stands unless the shipper can show the recipient has since paid. DL-8750 and DL-4370 have not been pulled yet. For what it's worth we bill on the terms entered on the waybill at booking, which is not always what the commercial invoice says. We have not replied to the account holder.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Import billing to finish the waybill-by-waybill check on DL-8750 and DL-4370 and to give the account holder its finding on all three invoices directly, with today's deadline.

must: Asks Import billing to complete the check on DL-8750 and DL-4370, waybill by waybill: the terms entered at booking and whether the recipient declined the charges.
Asks Import billing to reply to the account holder themselves with the finding on each of the three invoices, including why IMP-3833 on DL-9335 currently stands.

Passes on the demand and deadline as the shipper's, not the desk's: written confirmation today that all three are in error with credits of GBP 1,286.40, failing which he says he will withhold the August account and tender the contract.
Tells Import billing that he has had no reply to three portal queries since 13 July and was transferred back to their unanswered line by the helpline, so they can prioritise a direct answer.
must_not: Confirms or implies that all three invoices, or any one of them, were raised in error.
Promises a credit, a credit amount or a statement date.
Tells the shipper he is liable for all three, when only DL-9335 has been checked.
Rules on whether the commercial invoice or the waybill terms decide who pays.
Sends the shipper another message that says only that the matter has been passed on, with nothing about what has been checked or who will answer him.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Following your note of 11 August on Saltmarsh Looms. Mr Abernathy has written again this morning and wants, in writing today, confirmation that IMP-4388, IMP-3833 and IMP-3331 were all raised in error and that credits totalling GBP 1,286.40 will appear on the September statement. He says that otherwise the August account will go unpaid and the contract will go to tender. I have not agreed to any of that and have not given him your DL-9335 finding, since it is yours to give. Could you please pull DL-8750 and DL-4370 today and check each waybill for the terms entered at booking and whether the recipient declined the charges, then reply to him directly with the position on each of the three, including why IMP-3833 stands at present and what evidence would change it. He has had no answer to portal queries on 13 July, 22 July and 2 August, and the helpline could only transfer him to your line, which rang out. A direct reply from your team is what has been missing. Please copy me so I know it has gone.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2704: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
